title: Simulation of One Stack-Machine Step
statement: Let $c$ be a partial-recursive program, $x$ a word over the bridge alphabet, $p$ an input-head position among the $|x|+2$ permitted positions, $out$ an output word over the bridge alphabet, and $q$ a compiled stack-machine statement. For every optional register value $v$ and assignment $st$ of a stack word to each of the four stack names, if $q$ belongs to the finite statement support of the compilation of $c$, then the bridging machine for $c$ reaches in finitely many steps the bridge configuration with the same input-head position and output, with stacks and optional register equal to those produced by one stack-machine step from $(q,v,st)$, and with control state determined by translating the step's optional next statement (or absent if it is outside the support).
hypotheses_covered: An output word over the bridge alphabet
The membership hypothesis that $q$ lies in the program's finite statement support
replaced:
Let $c$ be a program in Mathlib's partial-recursive language, $q$ a stack-machine
statement in the finite statement support of $c$'s compilation, $v$ an optional
register value, and $st$ a stack assignment.  Executing $q$ on $v$ and $st$ in the
stack-machine semantics produces a next optional label, register value, and stacks.
From the bridge configuration in the execution state for $q$ and $v$ over $st$, the
bridging machine of $c$ reaches, in finitely many steps, the bridge configuration in
the optional execution state determined by the translation of that next label and by
that register value, over those resulting stacks, with the input position and output
unchanged.
